description: No skills are required, all are welcome. Designing a simple video game, kid friendly.
summary: I (we) developed a simple game, easy for young children to understand. Even though it is simple, it can still address the different factors that they should learn, to understand more about the difficulties of setting up and operating a lunar or Martian outpost. During the gameplay, it also teaches the player information, by giving the player freedom to make decisions based on the situations they are in.
details: The game helps players to learn sustainability through making decisions that bring about consequences. Even though it is simple, the game gets more challenging as the player progresses on. This allows young kids to learn more about Mars and the Moon, while also developing perseverance, as the player tries to beat his best survival score. Ultimately, the main lesson is about how the player manages to balance their resources, allowing for a steadier progress through questions that challenge them. Base44 was used for the project app, while Canva was used to help make the demo and presentation for this project. I (solo) considered adding songs, but unfortunately, it did not quite work out and I was not able to solve the problem. Even so, we worked around this and had to remove the music in the last minute, which was actually better compared to with music. The game had to be simple and kid-friendly, yet teaching the player more knowledge about establishing and maintaining a lunar or Martian outpost.
